sections.summary: Pharisees and scribes from Jerusalem challenge Jesus about his disciples eating with unwashed hands, invoking the tradition of the elders rather than Torah itself.

Jesus accuses the Pharisees of abandoning God's commandment in favor of human tradition, citing Isaiah 29:13 and illustrating with the Corban practice that allows a person to evade the duty of supporting parents.

Jesus declares that defilement comes from within the heart rather than from external contact, listing twelve internal sources of moral defilement; the author adds the interpretive note that Jesus thereby declared all foods clean.

A Gentile woman in the region of Tyre asks Jesus to heal her demon-possessed daughter; Jesus uses a metaphor of children's bread and dogs, the woman accepts the framework but argues from within it, and Jesus heals her daughter at a distance because of her answer.

sections.section_title: The Deaf Man with the Speech Impediment in the Decapolis
sections.summary: Jesus heals a deaf man with a speech impediment in the Decapolis through physical touch and the Aramaic command 'Ephphatha'; the Gentile crowd declares 'He has done all things well,' echoing Genesis 1:31 and fulfilling Isaiah 35:5-6.
